newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil dips $2 despite some EN590 demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil dips $2 despite some EN590 demand.

text.p: NWE gas oil slipped nearly $2 a tonne on Wednesday despite better demand for good quality EN590 cargoes, traders said.
Premiums for Rotterdam barges slipped 50 cents a tonne to trade at just 25 cents above the IPE for prompt loading. August IPE was down $1.75 at $174.50 at 1145 GMT.
"Sellers of prompt were aggressive this morning but for loadings at the end of the month you're probably talking close to $1 over," said a trader.
Cargoes were thinnly discussed although trade bids were 25 cents higher than Tuesday at $4.75 over the IPE for Aug EN590.
Bids for early September were heard at $6.00 above but some refiners were sceptical. "I'd like to test the $6 but won't have the oil," said one.
Further forward the swaps market remained well bid after a trader was heard buying some 250,000 tonnes of fourth quarter paper at $9 above the IPE on Tuesday.
"The inland demand in Germany is pretty poor at the moment but further forward there is clearly some demand," said a broker.
Russian cargoes were thinnly discussed around 75 cents above the IPE but there was little demand from blenders in Rotterdam.
